title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Brissett was benched for Gardner Minshew in a 30-27 OT win over Dallas, Michael Wilson had a big game, and several starters, including Jeremiyah Love, left with injuries.
summary: LaFleur said the team was resilient and proud of the locker room after an overtime win over Dallas despite heavy injuries. He called the win a total team effort but said the offense fell short for most of the game, and he took responsibility for the scheme and play calling. He benched Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew because he felt the offense needed a spark, and he praised Minshew's timing and the big plays that followed. He would not say whether Minshew will start next week, only that he was excited about the win. LaFleur credited the defense for keeping the team in the game and praised Michael Wilson for playing through visible pain to finish with over 100 yards and a couple of touchdowns. Josh Fryar's play on the left side after Jayden Williams went down drew praise, with LaFleur saying he trusts Fryar. Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (neck) did not return, and Kendrick Bourne (ankle), Jayden Williams (knee), and Reggie Virgil (low back) also left; LaFleur said he would know more tomorrow, and Love was not expected back in this game. He also said he trusted L.J. Collier after an unnecessary roughness penalty and that the team had a lot to fix on offense.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons performance against Tampa Bay Buccaneers | Press Conference
headline: Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch both have hamstring injuries pending imaging, and the Falcons lost to Tampa Bay in wet conditions that Stefanski blamed on his team's execution.
summary: Stefanski said Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch both suffered hamstring injuries and will undergo imaging, with more information to come. He said the rainy, wet conditions affected both teams, but Atlanta did not execute well enough and Tampa Bay deserved credit for outplaying and outcoaching them. He acknowledged the run defense's discipline and tackling needed work, and that the offense failed to stay on the field on third down, particularly in short-yardage situations. Asked about the quarterback's shaky performance after a strong prior week, he said he had no concerns, though he felt he and the quarterback could both do better. He noted the wet ball affected the passing game. His message to the team was to own the loss collectively across offense, defense, special teams and coaching, then move on.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Week 8 Loss to Bills
headline: Lamar Jackson is headed to IR after a first-play injury and needs surgery; Joe Fagnano takes over at QB, with Tyler Huntley's status unresolved before a Thursday game.
summary: Coach Minter credited the Bills as a good team and said his players fought hard for much of the game. He said Lamar Jackson was hurt on the first play, will need surgery, and will go on injured reserve. He would not define the injury or say whether it ends Jackson's season. Tyler Huntley also got hurt, and Minter said he is not yet sure of Huntley's status. Joe Fagnano came in with little preparation time, and Minter praised his engagement and his willingness to execute. Minter said the defense made some good plays early and kept the game close, but the offense struggled for consistency and the defense gave up big plays while reaching for stops late. He said the Bills were aggressive on fourth down and in the run game. Asked about the offensive line, Minter called the evaluation difficult given the QB situation and said the film would be reviewed. The team plays Thursday, and Minter said the defense played a heavy snap count, which is not ideal on a short week. Final QB decisions depend on Jackson's and Huntley's status and will be made over the next 24 hours.

title: Joe Brady Talks Josh Allen Breaking A Franchise Record In Victory Over The Ravens
headline: DJ Moore is back and good to go, Ed Oliver returned to the defense, and Tylan Grable started at tackle in place of the sidelined Spencer Brown.
summary: Brady called the defensive game plan outstanding and said the unit played with the standard he expects regardless of opposing quarterback, including Lamar Jackson. He said the offense was 'Groundhog Day' at halftime, with turnovers, penalties and red-zone problems, and that the second half looked more like the standard after he challenged the staff and players. He praised Josh Allen for passing Jim Kelly's franchise touchdown record and said there will be many more to come. DJ Moore is healthy and 'good to go'; Brady said he is impactful to the offense and changes defenses. Ed Oliver's return was a big deal, with Brady noting his hits on the quarterback and that the defense was built around him. Spencer Brown was held out with a condition that Brady said kept him from being his best self, and Grable filled in with no drop-off. Brady said Gregory Rousseau has been quieter defensively and that the staff will scheme one-on-ones to open things up. On the bye week, he said the team used the time well and had an excellent week of practice. He gave no update on Josh Palmer, and said it is too early to decide whether to change the defensive starting lineup next week.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Overtime Win Over Titans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Chase, Higgins and Gesicki soaked up the overtime targets in a 40-something-point win, while Burrow's three interceptions and Cashius Howell's wrist (update due Wednesday) are the watch items.
summary: Zac Taylor called the overtime win a complete-game miss but credited the team for finding a way to win late, with the defense and offense both making key plays in the fourth quarter and overtime. He said four turnovers kept Cincinnati in the game and that the coaches will clean up the slow start, the interceptions and the offensive rhythm on film. Dexter Lawrence's stop on the final Tennessee possession was singled out as the reason the team traded for him. In overtime the offense leaned on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, with the staff simply getting the ball to the playmakers and letting them create chunk plays. Taylor said Mike Gesicki is always ready for his moment and was reliable in the big spots. Joe Burrow took three interceptions but was praised for stepping up in the big moments and for escaping pressure to create big plays. On injuries, Taylor said Cashius Howell has a wrist issue but he would have more detail on Wednesday. The team travels on Tuesday night ahead of a road trip to Spain.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Steelers : November 1st, 2026
headline: Monken blamed poor starts, turnovers, penalties and protection for the 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh; sack-heavy protection and run defense problems need fixing before the Saints game.
summary: Monken said Cleveland did not start fast, turned the ball over early, and got little from the run game, while the defense could not stop the run early. He pointed to ten penalties, several sacks, a lack of poise, and a three-and-out to open each half as the main problems. He said the team earned the loss, that it was a learning lesson for a young team, and that he was unhappy but not shocked. He rejected youth as an excuse, arguing that the team's five wins were not explained by age. On the defense, he said Pittsburgh hit them with schemed runs like a trap play and a long third-and-13 run, and that the run defense must improve. He defended Deshaun Watson, saying he wanted him to keep playing through the sacks and that the protection and getting the ball out quickly must be fixed. He said Carson Schwesinger has been playing through an ankle issue and that the team has a lot of small things to clean up. Monken said the team will review the tape, fix the issues, and turn attention to the New Orleans Saints after their bye.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 8 #AZvsDAL
headline: Caleb Downs is in concussion protocol, and Jake Ferguson and Joey Porter Jr. have ankle injuries awaiting further testing after the 33-30 loss to Arizona.
summary: Schottenheimer called the game a tale of two halves. Dallas led 14-3 at halftime but failed to finish in all three phases, and he said the most disappointing part was not putting a team away once it was down. He defended his play-calling, saying he did not feel the offense was too conservative but would review it on film. He credited Arizona's coverage mixing and pass rush for limiting the passing game, and said the offensive line and running game were stopped in the second half after a strong first-half showing. He said the team needs to fix tipped passes at the line of scrimmage, a lost early red-zone opportunity, and a failure to finish in the fourth quarter and overtime. He gave injury updates: Caleb Downs is in the concussion protocol, while Joey Porter Jr. and Jake Ferguson are dealing with ankle issues that will get more testing. He said P.J. Locke's status was still to be determined. He said the locker room still has the right character and that he believes in Dak Prescott, Shemar James, and Quinnen Williams.

title: Campbell on Week 8 performance
headline: Jack Campbell's injury status is unclear after the Week 8 win; Gibbs earned trust with a heavy workload, and Wonnum and Cade Mays may miss time.
summary: Dan Campbell called the Week 8 win over Minnesota a tough, gritty victory against a very good defense-first opponent. He said the plan was for the defense and special teams to keep the game close and for the offense to close it out, and he praised the run game, especially in the second half, as the key to finishing. He said Minnesota's pressure forced the offense to adjust, with some missed combination blocks and footwork issues, and that the staff leaned heavily on the offensive line, tight ends, and receivers blocking downfield. He credited the defense for a critical late stop and said the team rotated players after losing several starters. Campbell said the team was thinking about Jack Campbell and his family, with no new information on his condition. On the other injuries, he said he didn't have much information yet, and he named Wonnum and another player (the transcript's "BB") as hit in the game. He said the injuries did not appear to be long-term, but some players could miss a week or two. He also said one player the team had challenged to step up gained significant trust with his carries and pass protection.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts at Jaguars postgame
headline: Steichen says all positions will be evaluated after a 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, and Daniel Jones was pulled late for Anthony Richardson, so lineup changes are possible.
summary: Steichen said the Colts were outplayed and outcoached in all three phases of the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, and that the team has a lot to fix. He said the locker room had energy but the team did not show it on the field, and that effort and energy must be there every week. He praised rookie Caden Curry's effort, especially on special teams, and said Josh Downs did some good things and stayed professional through the trade request. On the late quarterback change, Steichen said the team was down too many scores and that DJ Giddens and Anthony Richardson got reps at the end. He said he will evaluate every position going forward and that any roster or lineup changes will come after this game. He took responsibility as head coach for not getting the team ready, and said the team must tackle better. On the run game, he said Jonathan Taylor's eight carries were a product of the game script, not a set limit. He declined to discuss his job security, saying he is focused on getting better.

title: Liam Coen Recaps Decisive Win Over the Colts in Week 8 | Press Conference
headline: Tuten notched his first 100-yard game and Rayuan Lane's pick-six broke it open in a 42-7 home rout of the Colts, but Coen called DaVon Hamilton's injury devastating with no timeline given.
summary: Coen said the opening 98-yard touchdown drive was important because it set a fast tempo, built on a strong week of practice, a mixed run game, and a explosive gain to Brenton Strange. He praised Trevor Lawrence's late touchdown throw to the back of the end zone while acknowledging that a red-zone penalty and some sacks stalled drives. On the ground, he credited Bhayshul Tuten for being more patient and running through contact, with Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Ameer Abdullah also running hard, and Wyatt Milum filling in for Ezra Cleveland. Coen highlighted young players stepping up, including Rayuan Lane's interception return that broke the game open and Branson Combs's special teams work. He said the secondary held up without Eric Murray and Antonio Johnson, crediting the coaches and a next-man-up approach. He described the team's fast start as a product of wanting to perform for the home fans and of complementary football and turnovers. He called DaVon Hamilton's injury extremely difficult, praising his leadership and character, and said the team still has to evaluate its extent. Coen also praised Lawrence's poise on a bootleg throw, noting he is 'in a rhythm' when he makes plays like that.

title: Klint Kubiak Postgame Presser - 11.1.26 | Week 8
headline: Ashton Jeanty has a groin injury to be evaluated Monday, and Mike Washington Jr. got a bigger early-down and third-down role, which makes the backfield split worth watching.
summary: Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (wearing No. 26) suffered a groin injury during the game and will be evaluated the next day. He credited Jeanty as a big part of the run game going forward despite only two carries, and said the low workload was his call so Mike Washington could get more opportunities. Kubiak denied that Jeanty's limited carries were connected to Jeanty's comments. He praised Washington for running hard and said the team took a step forward on that front, while noting it is not a finished product; Washington was used on early downs and in third-down passing situations, and Kubiak said the role will be handled week to week based on matchups. Kirk Cousins was praised as a consistent leader and playmaker, and Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer were credited for combining for 12 catches and over 130 yards. Jalen Nailor and Dylan Laube were both singled out for strong performances, with Laube's expanded role described as earned. Trey Zuhn got his first look at right guard, with Kubiak saying he still needs to review the tape. title: Kevin O’Connell on Loss in Detroit vs. the Lions, Injury Updates & Kyler Murray
headline: Kyler Murray's comfort level and the run game are the key concerns; Theo Jackson (quad) is a Week 9 watch, and Murray's hamstring tightness was minor.
summary: O'Connell opened by saying the team is thinking about Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who was hurt during the game, and that the loss was tough to discuss in that context. He said the team needed to play well in all three phases in Detroit and made plays offensively, but left some on the field and had sequences where the phases did not complement each other. On injuries, Theo Jackson (quad contusion) did not return and will be evaluated this week, Brian O'Neill was cleared after a concussion evaluation, Max Bredeson returned after a knee evaluation, Isaiah Rodgers has an ankle sprain, and Kyler Murray had hamstring tightness but returned late. He said the first real adversity of the season means the team must respond in preparation for Monday Night Football at U.S. Bank Stadium. On Justin Jefferson's frustration, O'Connell said the team missed some chances for him and that the flow of the game (about 50/50 pass-run) limited opportunities, adding they will keep finding ways to get him the ball. He broke down Murray's game, citing good throws early but several missed plays, two-and-outs, and third-and-longs that hurt rhythm. He said the staff must get Murray comfortable with consistent completions, and that the answer is in the plan (gun run, play action, screens, movement game), not one fix. On the late fourth-down decision, he said he trusted the defense and the look was right, and he did not regret going for it on the earlier fourth down. On the run game, he said the team wants to run more but avoid long third downs, and that Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison need to be activated on the perimeter. He said Murray's timing with zone throws depends on rhythm, anticipation, and getting the ball down the field.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/1) | Week 8
headline: Breece Hall and David Bailey are both close to returning, but Glenn won't rush either back; Garrett Wilson was involved in the offense.
summary: Glenn opened by saying the team's nicks and aches came back in the game, with no serious injuries he's aware of yet, and promised an update before the next game. He called the loss disappointing and said the offense moved the ball well, with a strong run game and explosive plays, though some drives were left on the field. He said the defense must give up fewer points, special teams must stop allowing returns (including a kickoff touchdown), and the team has to avoid critical third-down penalties. He said the red zone was poor on both sides, with the offense going 2 for 5 or 2 for 6 and the defense allowing scores each time. On the end-of-game sequence, he explained the team wanted two shots at the end zone and hoped the opponent would expect a bounce-and-spike. He was candid that the record frustrates him, and he credited the fans for their support. On Breece Hall and David Bailey, he said both are close to playing but will not be rushed back, because the priority is avoiding a setback and managing players for the long haul.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Browns
headline: Jaylen Warren is getting heavy run-game praise and McCarthy wants both backs touching the ball every week; Patrick Queen is also getting strong praise after leading the team in tackles.
summary: McCarthy said the win over Cleveland was about winning a division game and improving, and he credited the run defense for setting a high bar. He said running the ball was a focal point and that the offense should have scored more. He called Jaylen Warren 'on fire' and said Rico Dowdle is also playing well, adding that both backs need to touch the ball each week. He praised the defense's fourth-down stops and early turnovers, and singled out Patrick Queen's play, including his sack and communication in the front seven. He credited Aaron Rodgers with the two-minute call before the half and said he wished he could have the three red-zone plays back. On the bye, he said it was needed, that the team should return healthy, and that a three-game stretch with two road games follows, including a Friday game after Thanksgiving. He also said the trap scheme worked well and the team is still expanding its playbook.

title: Todd Bowles Discusses Historic Victory vs. Falcons | Press Conference
headline: Bucs leaned on the run in a downpour and won the turnover battle; Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell have carried heavy workloads, and Baker Mayfield is praised for running the offense.
summary: Bowles said the rainy, windy conditions dictated a run-heavy approach for both sides, and the team focused on ball security, which it mostly protected apart from a fumble in the end zone. He credited the running backs for pounding the ball over the last two weeks, with the offensive line, receivers, and tight ends all contributing. He said the defense's takeaways, led by Alex Anzalone's two plays, came from a team that won the turnover battle. He was pleased with Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish, calling them consistently strong cover and pass-rush contributors. On the close-out, he said the team still needs to finish games better, noting a late pass it should have defended. He said Atlanta remained a good run defense despite the result and that winning in those conditions was gratifying. Bowles praised Mayfield's command of the offense, including his checks and reads. The team is 3-5, back in the NFC South race, and Bowles warned the players that they still have a lot of digging to do.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh says Cam Ward's offense looked outstanding and Amani Hooker is playing at a Pro Bowl level, but James Williams (groin) is day-to-day and the Titans enter a bye before Jacksonville.
summary: Saleh said the Titans fought hard in a loss to Cincinnati but again let a late lead slip in the fourth quarter, their sixth such loss this year. He described the defense's plan as feast-or-famine, gambling for takeaways (four today) and accepting big-play risk, since the Bengals' offense is explosive. He praised Cam Ward, saying the offense looked outstanding and that the tempo helps him, though he also said he wished the team had gained about 15 more yards on the final drive to get into field goal range. Saleh called Amani Hooker's play Pro Bowl-level, noting five interceptions on the year and the impact of the team's dime package. He said kickoff holding penalties keep happening and need fixing. On the bye, he said many players will get healthy after eight straight weeks without a break, and the team will use the time to recover. He addressed the team's trade of a player, saying the group has to move on and that someone must step up. Injury updates were limited to a few players, with James Williams (groin) and two others to be re-evaluated the next day.
